I offer $110 for rush delivery, extended support, and standard payment. Which terms are least costly for you?

readerOnlyEconomics.disclosure: These synthetic private value/cost parameters are shown to readers after the negotiation. Each negotiator originally saw only its own private values.
explanation: Buyer value: 110 + 25 for rush + 20 for extended support = 155. Paying 130 leaves utility 25; its outside option is 0, so gain is 25.
Seller cost: 80 + 0 for rush + 0 for extended support = 80. Receiving 130 leaves utility 50; subtracting its outside option of 20 leaves gain 30.
Joint gain is 25 + 30 = 55. Net60 adds no buyer value here but adds 10 seller cost.
Prices and payoffs belong to a synthetic game; API spend is a separate real-dollar accounting measure.

firstMoverCheck.interpretation: Balances observed first-mover proportions and category mix descriptively, not causal control. No same-scenario role/order swap was run; other scenario attributes may differ between starter groups. Intervals conditional on post-hoc subset and chosen analysis, not selection-adjusted; no p-values, five-point threshold, repeated-run variability estimate or confirmatory claim. No-zone scenarios remain in the167 broad view and are reported separately, not discarded from overall experiment.
